description:
SPECTRUM returns with the second instalment of its No Monochrome series, welcoming label debutants Jochem Hamerling, and Ae:ther & Vicius, alongside returning favourite Kaufmann for another forward- thinking collection of club material.

Launched in 2024, the No Monochrome series debuted with standout contributions from Mitch de Klein, Rob Hes, Cyantist, and SHMN, setting the tone for a VA concept built around depth, energy, and individuality. Volume two continues that vision with three expansive cuts that each carve out their own distinct atmosphere.

Kaufmann returns to the label following her acclaimed 'Space Sheriff' appearance with 'Fluppe'. Dark, hypnotic, and unpredictable, the track rides on a nasty synth hook, trippy vocal textures, and a pounding kick drum, delivering another immersive trip from the German producer.

Ae:ther and Vicius combine forces on 'Roar' , a track that lives up to its name from the very first beat. Built around a deep, guttural synth line and wrapped in sweeping emotive strings, the record surges forward in powerful waves, rising and collapsing with seismic intensity. It's a dramatic and cinematic soundtrack designed for big-room moments and late-night tension alike.

Closing the latest volume is longtime friend Jochem Hamerling with 'Moves Ya.' A rolling, acid tinged cut built around a snarling synth line, weighty low-end, and groove-led rhythm. Elevated by chords and a pounding kick drum, the track maintains a restless energy throughout, making it the perfect finale to another standout chapter in the No Monochrome series.

title: Turn The Tide
description:

Dimitri Vegas and Pat B have taken a trip down memory lane with their remake of Syler’s 2001 dance classic, Turn The Tide. The track has elements of the new school hardstyle style whilst still retaining the emotion of the original track.

Turn The Tide ventures through nostalgic nods to early dance music, with Syler’s original vocals echoing amongst powerful bass stabs and whirring progressive chords. The track brings together audiences of all ages and backgrounds, uniting the dance floor through euphoric build-ups and hard-hitting drops that shake the speakers. Dimitri ‘Vegas’ Thivaios is a Belgian DJ, producer, and actor best known as half of the world-renowned electronic duo Dimitri Vegas & Like Mike. description:
The Wayout · C minor · 171 BPM
A love letter to the alternative music I grew up with.

I worked on this track on and off for about a year, pulling together the sounds that shaped me — 80s/90s post-punk, alternative, indie and new romantic, with a dose of synthwave thrown into the mix.

Think; Cure-inspired basslines, thrashy Placebo-esque guitars, washed-out shoegaze textures and synths underneath it all. Dark, energetic and a little melodramatic — for those times when nothing is actually wrong, but you’re so bored you almost wish there was something bigger to be goth about.

This was also the first track I sent out for professional mixing and mastering. I was fortunate enough to work with Dan Konopka of OK Go, who mixed the track and also laid down new drums.

Built from a combination of my own soft synths, Splice samples and adapted/rearranged vocal samples.

title: Unaccomplished
description:
You can have proof that your life is moving forward and still feel behind.

“Unaccomplished” lives in that contradiction.

You paid what needed paying.
Changed what needed changing.
Showed up when you were tired.
Helped the people you love.
Built things you once prayed for.

Then somehow the finish line moved again.

The record starts with the pressure we put on ourselves, moves into the receipts of everything we've actually accomplished, then asks a harder question:

What happens when “doing more” follows you into your relationships too?

Sometimes somebody isn't asking you to solve another problem.

They're asking you to hear them.
They're asking you to stay.

Maybe being unaccomplished isn't always about how little you've done.

Maybe it's about never deciding what “enough” actually means.

OnHoodie Productions
Where Pain Has a Sound.

“Broken Pieces” by Freq 10 featuring Frequency X is a dark, intimate contemporary R&B slow burn about loving again after emotional damage.

Five distinct voices move through fear, trust, survival, and healing, building from exposed solo moments into rich five part harmony. Deep bass, smoky electric piano, atmospheric synths, muted guitar, and cinematic strings create a mature sound that recalls the emotional honesty of Jodeci, the vocal precision of Boyz II Men, the sensual restraint of Maxwell, and the atmospheric edge of Prince’s Minneapolis Sound.

This is not a song about being rescued. It is about recognizing that every scar has a story and every broken piece still belongs.
